diagrams.title: Choose the Buyer Before the File Format
diagrams.subtitle: Research the problem, create a useful product, connect the offer, and make delivery understandable.
diagrams.caption: Victor Jaro emphasizes buyer research; Baddie In Business demonstrates Canva production; Rochelle Be connects a free win to a paid offer; Richard Yu simplifies sales links; Tatyana Savage supplies access instructions.
diagrams.assumptions_note: These practitioners describe complementary practices, not a jointly operated business or a guaranteed sales sequence.
diagrams.note: Jaro reports no sales from their first student-and-teacher templates. Savage describes instructions in listing images and delivered files as a way to reduce customer questions.

stages.label: Research the buyer
stages.detail: Victor Jaro researches the buyer and topic before investing hours in a paid Notion template.

stages.label: Build the useful product
stages.detail: Baddie In Business duplicates a working Canva page layout and exports the ebook as PDF standard.

stages.label: Connect a small win
stages.detail: Rochelle Be makes the freebie goal-specific and outcome-focused, with a direct connection to the paid product.

stages.label: Simplify the purchase path
stages.detail: Richard Yu links a single product directly to its sales page and recommends at most three intermediate links when several offers are available.

stages.label: Explain access and usage
stages.detail: Tatyana Savage puts download instructions and FAQs in listing images and usage instructions inside the delivered files.

diagrams.title: From a $7 Entry Product to a $57 Bundle
diagrams.subtitle: Related products expand the order; delivery must match what the buyer actually purchases.
diagrams.caption: Maik Kleinert | Content-to-Conversion Systems describes a $7 entry product, a mini course reduced to $20, and another product reduced to $30, producing a $57 order.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Maik Kleinert's amounts are product prices and the reported combined order, not audience counts or conversion rates. The first three amounts are individual line items, not running subtotals. The final amount repeats at delivery.
diagrams.note: Maik Kleinert checks whether a promotional DM was already sent and whether the person already purchased. Funnel Building Secrets recommends placing a test order through checkout and the additional offers.

stages.label: Entry product
stages.detail: Maik Kleinert identifies the entry product as the starting offer in the DM-connected product bundle.

stages.label: Mini-course addition
stages.detail: Maik Kleinert describes reducing the mini course from $27 to $20.

stages.label: Related product addition
stages.detail: Maik Kleinert describes reducing the other product from $47 to $30.

stages.label: Combined order
stages.conversion: Applies when all three products are bought
stages.detail: Maik Kleinert reports that the combined purchase is $57 rather than the $7 entry purchase alone.

stages.label: Purchased-product delivery
stages.detail: Keep access tied to the purchased products. Funnel Building Secrets calls for a test order to confirm the purchase path works.

diagrams.title: Separate Sale Price, Proceeds, and Commission
diagrams.subtitle: Reported checkout examples clarify what a template seller can compare without treating commission as the full cost.
diagrams.caption: Stack Receipts reports a $20 domestic-card sale leaving $18.50 through Lemon Squeezy or $18.12 through Payhip Free after Stripe. Smart Capital reports a $2.90 Gumroad commission on a $29 template before processing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each total starts an independent checkout example. Stack Receipts supplies the proceeds directly; no intermediate fee amounts are estimated. Smart Capital's final deduction is commission only, and no Gumroad net payout is asserted.
diagrams.note: These Stack Receipts and Smart Capital storefront examples apply to template checkout planning. Job4all separately reports Notion Marketplace charges of 8% plus $0.40; those charges must not be applied to these other platforms.

diagrams.title: Price the Specific Result
diagrams.subtitle: Beginner downloads, edited PDFs, and a resource-app bundle carry different practitioner price recommendations.
diagrams.caption: Baddie In Business suggests $9–$27 beginner downloads. Richard Yu recommends $27–$47 for an edited, pain-specific PDF. Nathan Nazareth demonstrates a $39 one-time guide, member area, and AI resource-app offer.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Baddie In Business and Richard Yu provide range endpoints, not observed price distributions. Each endpoint is shown separately with identical minimum, maximum, and reference values; none is asserted to be a statistical typical price.
diagrams.note: Nathan Nazareth puts the offer before the product and recommends testing the published app through a real credit-card purchase after functional cleanup.
diagrams.unit: USD per offer; fixed reference points

diagrams.title: Choose the Payment Route Before Migrating
diagrams.subtitle: Check eligibility, tax responsibility, product operations, and payout timing before relying on a replacement checkout.
diagrams.caption: Gaurav Tiwari prioritizes seller eligibility and license keys; SoloBuild compares tax administration and payout terms; OCH Platform distinguishes Stripe Tax activation from a Stripe connection; heyymilian identifies missing product-delivery functions.
diagrams.assumptions_note: These are Gaurav Tiwari, SoloBuild, OCH Platform, and heyymilian's reported checks. Eligibility, coverage, and pricing depend on the provider and product configuration; a payment connection alone does not establish tax handling.
diagrams.note: Gaurav Tiwari recommends retaining control of the customer list, license server, and checkout links. SoloBuild reports a $100 Paddle payout minimum and monthly payment by the fifteenth.

nodes.question: Does the destination accept the seller location and intended product?
nodes.fail_action: Choose an eligible destination before migrating. Gaurav Tiwari reports that their India-based plugin business is excluded from the Managed Payments path they discuss.

nodes.question: Are tax responsibility, coverage, and the administrative trade-off understood?
nodes.fail_action: Compare filing time and accountant costs with the handoff premium as SoloBuild recommends. For the Stripe Tax route, follow OCH Platform's separate dashboard and integration activation.

nodes.question: Are delivery, license keys, download links, storefront functions, and affiliates accounted for?
nodes.fail_action: Arrange the missing functions before switching. heyymilian says Managed Payments does not include these Lemon Squeezy functions; Gaurav Tiwari puts existing license keys ahead of promotional fees.

nodes.question: Do payout timing and minimum balances fit the business?
nodes.pass_next: Proceed with the eligible route and the accounted-for delivery and licensing arrangements.
nodes.fail_action: Reconsider the provider or cash timing before depending on payouts. SoloBuild reports Paddle's monthly schedule and $100 minimum.

diagrams.title: Build the Newsletter Around a Reader Problem
diagrams.subtitle: Connect positioning, repeatable publishing, suitable advertising, and outcome-led offers.
diagrams.caption: Nicolas Cole emphasizes positioning and discovery; beehiiv demonstrates repeatable production and advertising operations; Write • Build • Scale develops reader conversations; Matt McGarry connects cohort assignments to promised outcomes.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Nicolas Cole, beehiiv, Write • Build • Scale, and Matt McGarry describe operating practices, not a shared staffing structure. The functions do not imply separate employees, and publisher headcount is not specified.
diagrams.note: beehiiv reports up to five claimed advertising offers at once and five days to publish. Stack Receipts advises comparing advertising earnings with the plan bill at the same list size and billing cadence.

center.focus: Serve a specific reader problem with a repeatable publication and relevant paid outcomes, following Nicolas Cole and Write • Build • Scale.

spokes.kpi: Reader acquisition by source; Nicolas Cole reports over 50% of Write With AI's acquisition came from inside Substack's ecosystem.
A repeatable issue format and publishing routine; beehiiv's Dope Act example saves the drafting process as a Claude skill.
Suitable placements within beehiiv's reported five-day claim window; reject unsuitable offers with a reason.
Assignments sufficient for the promised outcome, as Matt McGarry requires; use reader conversations about goals and obstacles as Write • Build • Scale recommends.

diagrams.title: Compare Base Rates Without Hiding Other Charges
diagrams.subtitle: Percentage charges are only one part of the storefront decision.
diagrams.caption: Smart Capital reports 10% Gumroad commission and 5% on Payhip Free. Stack Receipts uses 5% plus $0.50 for Lemon Squeezy. Job4all reports 8% plus $0.40 for Notion Marketplace.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Smart Capital, Stack Receipts, and Job4all describe separate platform alternatives. The percentages are not additive, the low and high values repeat each quoted base rate, and fixed charges and processing are not converted into invented effective-rate estimates.
diagrams.note: Smart Capital explicitly separates commission from processing. Stack Receipts specifies a domestic-card example. Job4all also mentions foreign exchange and possible refund or chargeback costs. These reported schedules are not promises of current platform terms.
diagrams.unit: Percent of sale; independent platform alternatives
diagrams.total_range: Quoted base percentage rates span 5%–10%; do not sum the alternatives

buckets.label: Gumroad commission
buckets.notes: Smart Capital reports 10%, equivalent to $2.90 on its $29 template example, before processing.

buckets.label: Payhip Free platform charge
buckets.notes: Smart Capital reports 5%, equivalent to $1.45 on its $29 example, before processing.

buckets.label: Lemon Squeezy base percentage
buckets.notes: Stack Receipts applies 5% plus $0.50 to its $20 domestic-card example and reports $18.50 in proceeds.

buckets.label: Notion Marketplace percentage
buckets.notes: Job4all reports 8% plus $0.40 per transaction, with foreign-exchange and possible refund or chargeback costs discussed separately.

diagrams.title: Connect Faceless Content to a Working Purchase Path
diagrams.subtitle: Choose the buyer problem, demonstrate the product, connect checkout, and distinguish attention from sales.
diagrams.caption: Nick Nyxson and Nataleh Nicole connect useful content to relevant offers; Success With Sam demonstrates screen recordings; Rochelle Be checks generated video; Brem tests checkout links; DIGITAL INCOME PROJECT separates audience growth from monetization.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The weekly slots organize these practitioners' actions without imposing production quotas. Nick Nyxson, Nataleh Nicole, Success With Sam, Rochelle Be, and Brem do not establish a shared four-week completion or revenue promise.
diagrams.note: DIGITAL INCOME PROJECT reports 10,000 followers and over 500,000 views in 30 days while stating that monetization is still being tested. Richard Yu warns that affiliate refunds can remove commissions.

weeks.title: Choose the problem and relevant offer
weeks.deliverable: A buyer problem and an offer that useful content can demonstrate, following Nick Nyxson and Nataleh Nicole.
weeks.gate: For affiliate offers, read buyer feedback and try the product where possible, as Richard Yu recommends before risking audience trust.

weeks.title: Produce and inspect the demonstration
weeks.deliverable: A screen-recorded product demonstration in the style shown by Success With Sam, with main search keywords in the title and curiosity in the thumbnail as Nataleh Nicole recommends.
weeks.gate: Preview generated video and correct misplaced overlays or awkward text before publication, following Rochelle Be.

weeks.title: Connect the content to checkout
weeks.deliverable: A description with the relevant product link and a connected purchase button. One Person Business places the offer link at the top of the description.
weeks.gate: Press the live-preview purchase button and confirm the intended checkout opens, as Brem does with Gumroad embedded in Framer.

weeks.title: Separate audience traction from sales
weeks.deliverable: Separate audience and purchase observations, following DIGITAL INCOME PROJECT's distinction between reach and monetization.
weeks.gate: Do not treat follower or view counts as product sales. DIGITAL INCOME PROJECT explicitly leaves monetization under test after reporting audience growth.
